title: Andaman Islands
overview_paragraphs:
This trip covers the Andaman Islands' three main hubs in six nights, from Port Blair's wartime history to Havelock's blue-flag beaches and Neil Island's coral-formed bridges, moving by ferry between islands with a mix of relaxation, snorkeling, and water sports built in.

Best for travelers who want beach time, water activities, and a touch of colonial-era history in one island-hopping trip.

places.name: Port Blair
places.tagline: The Andamans' historic gateway, marked by a colonial-era jail.
places.desc: Port Blair opens and closes the trip, centered on the Cellular Jail, a former British penal colony turned into an evening Light & Sound Show retelling its history after dark. Nearby, North Bay and Ross Island add a different side of the city's past and present, Ross Island's ruins tracing its Japanese and British-era history, while North Bay's coral reefs turn the same stretch of water into a base for scuba diving, snorkeling, parasailing, and glass-bottom boat rides.

places.name: Havelock Island
places.tagline: Home to Radha Nagar, one of Asia's most awarded beaches.
places.desc: Havelock holds the trip's best-known stretch of sand: Radha Nagar Beach, Blue Flag-certified and known for calm, clear water suited to swimming and relaxation. Elephanta Beach (also called Coral Beach) adds the island's water-sport side, reached by a small shared boat and known for snorkeling, jet skiing, and banana boat rides just offshore.

places.name: Neil Island
places.tagline: Coral beaches and a bridge shaped entirely by nature.
places.modal_tagline: THE QUIETER, SLOWER ISLAND OF THE THREE
places.desc: Neil Island runs at a gentler pace, built around Bharatpura Beach's shallow, swim-friendly water and Laxmanpura Beach's white sand and sunset views. Its signature sight is the Natural Bridge, a rock formation shaped entirely by coral growth over time and best seen at low tide, when the arch is fully exposed.
